reasoning: Recent public and private polling over the last ~45 days consistently shows Republican Kurt Alme leading in the 2026 Montana Senate race, particularly in the current multi‑candidate configuration where Democrat Alani Bankhead and independent Seth Bodnar split the anti‑Republican vote. In full-field three- or four-way scenarios, Alme typically leads by mid- to high double digits (roughly R+15 to R+25), while a hypothetical consolidated anti‑Alme field (especially Bodnar vs. Alme head‑to‑head) produces much smaller Republican leads or even a narrow Bodnar advantage, implying a structural environment around R+10–R+15 but a current effective margin closer to **R+20** under existing ballot conditions.

sources.name: Breitbart summarizing GrayHouse Poll
sources.details: GrayHouse poll of likely voters finds Alme at 41%, Bankhead 25%, Bodnar 17% in a three-way, implying roughly an R+16 lead over the nearest opponent.

sources.name: PollsMax Montana Senate Forecast
sources.details: PollsMax forecast using Tavern Research head‑to‑head polling shows a statewide Senate polling average of 52.0% R to 48.0% I, an R+4 environment in that two-way configuration.

sources.name: PollsMax Montana Senate Polling Average
sources.details: PollsMax aggregate of Montana Senate polling with Bodnar as the main non‑Republican shows 41.9% R to 20.4% I, an R+21.4 average in that framing, though Democrats are not modeled as the principal alternative.

sources.name: Bullfinch poll as reported by Polling USA
sources.details: Bullfinch survey of likely voters reports Alme 36%, Bodnar 24%, Bankhead 22% in a three-way contest, implying approximately an R+12 lead over the nearest non‑Republican.

sources.name: Tavern Research Montana Senate Poll
sources.details: Tavern Research poll finds Alme at 49%, Bodnar 25%, Bankhead 24%, Austin 2% in a full-field race, amounting to an R+24 advantage over the nearest opponent; head‑to‑head tests show Alme 51–49 vs Bodnar and 59–41 vs Bankhead.

sources.name: Independent Center Voice & Independent Leadership Council Survey
sources.details: Independent Center Voice / Independent Leadership Council benchmark survey of 793 likely voters finds Alme 36%, Bodnar 24%, Bankhead 22% with 17% unsure, mirroring the Bullfinch pattern and suggesting an R+12 lead.

sources.name: Washington Reporter summary of NRSC Montana Senate Poll
sources.details: NRSC internal polling obtained by Washington Reporter shows Alme at 45%, Bankhead 30%, Bodnar 15% in a three-way (R+15 over Bankhead) and finds Alme leading 49–46 vs Bankhead and 50–43 vs Bodnar in separate head‑to‑head matchups.

sources.name: Breitbart summary of NRSC Montana Senate Poll
sources.details: Breitbart story on Bodnar’s potential exit recaps the same NRSC polling: Alme 45%, Bankhead 30%, Bodnar 15% in a three-way and Alme ahead of both Bankhead and Bodnar in head‑to‑head tests, reinforcing an R+15 multi‑candidate margin.

sources.name: Strength In Numbers Montana Senate Poll (reported by G. Elliott Morris)
sources.details: Strength In Numbers / G. Elliott Morris–reported poll finds Bodnar would lead Alme 50–44 in a head‑to‑head, while Bankhead would lose 44–52; in the current four‑way race Alme still wins with 41%, illustrating that consolidation is required to erase Alme’s advantage.

sources.name: Daily Montanan overview of Montana Senate polling
sources.details: Daily Montanan synthesis of limited polling notes Alme is "almost assured to win by double digits" in three‑way scenarios, with Bankhead only slightly ahead of Bodnar and analysts rating the seat Solid Republican.

sources.name: Flathead Beacon synthesis of Montana Senate polling
sources.details: Flathead Beacon reports internal and public surveys showing Bankhead and Bodnar splitting around 45–49% while Alme hovers just above 40%, implying that with consolidation the race could tighten to mid‑single digits but that the current split maintains a comfortable GOP edge.

sources.name: Cook Political Report PVI – Montana
sources.details: Cook Political Report’s Partisan Voting Index rates Montana as R+11 statewide, indicating a structurally Republican-leaning environment in federal races.
sources.date_range: Various 2024 elections; structural rating current as of 2024 cycle
